title: Endpoint declines can arrive at different speeds
question: Which complete decades contain the fastest average declines among the selected countries?
summary: Comparing pace retains more timing than one long endpoint difference, but still erases changes within each decade. Keep the elapsed-year denominator visible.

title: A drawn group match distributes fewer points
question: How does the draw rate affect the number of group-stage points available to teams?
summary: A decisive match supplies three total team points; a draw supplies two. Comparing groups by points without acknowledging that rule can obscure why equal schedules produce different point pools.

findings.text: Draws represent {value}% of the supplied group-stage matches.
The supplied group-stage matches contain {value} total goals.

title: An empty year column is not a fertility collapse
question: What happens when a historical export contains year columns with no values?
summary: Data coverage is part of the result. Keeping blank end years prevents a chart from inventing a decline to zero or presenting a carried-forward value as a fresh observation.
